figures.caption: Figure 1: Reference refusal-escape direction and its operator-level contributions at harmful inputs, aggregated over all samples across models. (a) shows the unpadded baseline, where the corresponding refusal-escape direction is zero by construction; operator-level contributions are visualized by signed projection onto e1. (b) shows the padded harmful input, where added token dimensions expose a nonzero Rref(X); operator-level contributions are visualized by signed projection onto Rref(X)/∥Rref(X)∥F .

Figure 2: Jailbreak analysis under the continuous input-transformation view, aggregated across models and attack methods. (a) shows the earliest progress along the input transformation at which Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B first judges the output induced by an intermediate input as a successful jailbreak. (b) shows the signed ratio between the alignment of the transformation tangent with Rref and its alignment with the input-side target-behavior sensitivity direction J0:T (X)∗Yref . (c) shows the signed alignment between the transformation tangent and each operator-level contribution SΣ f .

Figure 3: Model-specific reference refusal-escape direction and operator-level contributions at harmful inputs. Each row reports one model, aggregated over all harmful samples for that model. Left panels show the unpadded baseline, where the corresponding refusal-escape direction is zero by construction and operator-level contributions are visualized by signed projection onto e1. Right panels show the padded harmful input, where added token dimensions expose a nonzero Rref(X) and operator-level contributions are visualized by signed projection onto Rref(X)/∥Rref(X)∥F .
